note.headline: Alphabet: sales accelerate, cash flow collapses; price sits under resistance near 300

summary.thesis: Alphabet's sales are growing faster, but free cash flow has fallen hard and analysts expect lower profit next year, so the price already assumes a lot.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price or a recovery in cash flow. Swing: wait, because the price is pressing into a ceiling with no clear trend.

note.happening: GOOGL closed at 298.7, up 1.79% on the day. That puts it just under a resistance zone at 300.07–305.86, a level where sellers have shown up before, and still below its falling 50-day average of 329.12. Today's news was about products: a confirmed Search upgrade, and a reported outage that some Google users said affected them. There is no earnings date in the data.
note.business: The things that change the business point in different directions. Demand is strong: quarterly sales grew 24.65% from a year earlier, up from 21.79% two quarters ago, and trailing sales reached 471.1B against 385.5B a year before. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. Cash is the problem. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, which is a 4.19% margin. Heavy investment is the usual explanation for a drop like this (general knowledge), but the data does not break the spending down. Net margin of 50.03% is above the operating margin, so reported profit includes gains from outside the core business. That flatters the trailing P/E of 15.7. Analysts expect EPS of 14.97 next year against 19.56 this year, and they cut this year's estimate by 5.2% over 30 days. Today's Search news and the reported outage affect sentiment, not the numbers. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 139.0B and liquidity is 265.1B. What is at risk is how much cash the company makes and whether profit forecasts hold.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree sharply. A discounted cash flow model values a company by the cash it will produce. Built on today's 19.7B of free cash flow, it gives 26.28 to 72.2 per share, with a base of 52.56. Even assuming 30% starting growth, it reaches only 80.15. Measured against its own past price-to-sales ratios, the stock looks fair: 234.35 at the low end, 282.31 in the middle, 375.22 at the high end. The price-to-sales ratio of 7.8 is above the peer median of 5.4 and sits at the 54.0 percentile of its own five-year range. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: whether free cash flow stays near 19.7B or returns toward the 73.6B of a year ago. The data's own risk note says the price needs about 37% yearly growth, against 17% delivered over three years. My range is 234.35 to 282.31, which puts the current 298.7 above it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the prior 73.6B once the current investment cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: quarterly growth was 24.65%, up from 21.79% two quarters ago.
Margins are widening: operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%.
The balance sheet is strong, with 139.0B of net cash and 265.1B of liquidity to fund investment.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, and the cash-flow model's base value is 52.56 per share.
Forecasts are falling: this year's EPS estimate was cut 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's EPS of 14.97 is below this year's 19.56.
The stock costs more than its peers: price-to-sales is 7.8 against a peer median of 5.4.

longterm.why: The business earns a quality grade of B, but at 298.7 the price is above my range while forecasts fall. A pullback toward 282.31, or clear signs of a free-cash-flow recovery, would improve the trade-off.

swing.why: The price sits just under resistance at 300.07–305.86 and below falling 20-day and 50-day averages, and the trend is a range. The nearest support below is 293.72–296.49, so the setup has no clear edge either way.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, timing depends on forecast revisions and price levels. Options price a move of about 4.2% by Nov 20 and 8.0% by Dec 18, and the busiest put strike, 290.0, marks a level traders are watching.

change_mind: Free cash flow climbs back clearly toward the prior 73.6B in a coming filing, which would lift the cash-flow value well above 52.56.
The price falls into the 275.72–278.27 support zone and holds, which puts it inside my fair-value range.
The price closes above the 309.73–314.7 resistance zone (5 touches) while EPS estimate cuts stop, which would turn the range into an uptrend.
note.what_changed: The price rose 1.79% to 298.7 and is now above the 293.72–296.49 zone that yesterday's note called resistance, but forecasts, cash flow and valuation are unchanged, so the view stays at wait.
